requirements.text:
clamp(x, lo, hi) reads its arguments as signed integers. It returns lo when x < lo, else hi
when x > hi, else x.
requirements.reason: The statement uses signed comparisons and returns lo when x < lo, otherwise hi when x > hi, otherwise x, exactly as required. The examples also confirm signed interpretation, such as 4294967295 representing −1.

requirements.text:
gcd(a, b) reads its arguments as unsigned integers and returns their greatest common divisor,
with gcd(a, 0) = a.
requirements.reason: The statement computes the unsigned greatest common divisor for every pair of inputs; in particular, gcd(a, 0) = a. The result fits in 32 bits, so reducing it modulo 2³² does not change it.

requirements.text: sum_to(n) reads n as an unsigned integer and returns 0 + 1 + ... + (n - 1), wrapped to 32 bits.
requirements.reason: The statement sums the unsigned values from 0 through n−1 and returns the result modulo 2³², including for every 32-bit input.

claims.summary: For every 32-bit input, sum_to returns the sum of the integers from zero up to but not including the input, modulo 32 bits.
claims.name: Examples.Toy.sumTo
claims.intent: `sum_to(n)` on unsigned 32-bit ints: `0 + 1 + … + (n − 1)`, wrapped to 32 bits.
details: Covers every 32-bit input n, interpreted as an unsigned natural number from zero through the maximum 32-bit value.
The returned value is the sum of all integers from zero up to, but not including, n, reduced modulo 2 to the 32nd power.
Returns also guarantees the module is instantiable, and that every call in every fresh instance and host behavior terminates without trapping or throwing and returns exactly the specified result.

claims.summary: For all 32-bit inputs, clamp returns the lower bound if the input is below it, the upper bound if the input is above it, and otherwise the input, using signed comparisons.
claims.statement:
∀ (x lo hi : BitVec 32),
  FVA.Wasm.Exec.Returns Examples.Toy.Lifted.module "clamp"
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 x, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 lo, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 hi]
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 (if x.slt lo = true then lo else if hi.slt x = true then hi else x)]
claims.name: Examples.Toy.clamp
claims.intent:
`clamp(x, lo, hi)` on signed 32-bit ints: `lo` if `x < lo`, else `hi` if `x > hi`, else `x`
(tested in this order, so with `lo > hi` the result is `lo` for `x < lo` and `hi` otherwise).
details: Covers every combination of three 32-bit inputs: x, lo, and hi.
Comparisons interpret the inputs as signed two's-complement integers; the returned value is one of the original 32-bit inputs, without arithmetic wraparound.
Returns also guarantees the module is instantiable, and that every call in every fresh instance and host behavior terminates without trapping or throwing and returns exactly the specified result.
caveats: This is a signed comparison clamp, but the claim does not require the lower bound to be less than or equal to the upper bound; when they are reversed, the nested comparison still determines the returned value.

claims.summary: For every pair of 32-bit inputs, gcd returns their unsigned greatest common divisor as a 32-bit value.
claims.statement:
∀ (a b : BitVec 32),
  FVA.Wasm.Exec.Returns Examples.Toy.Lifted.module "gcd" [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 a, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 b]
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 (BitVec.ofNat 32 (a.toNat.gcd b.toNat))]
claims.name: Examples.Toy.gcd
claims.intent: `gcd(a, b)` on unsigned 32-bit ints: their greatest common divisor (`gcd(a, 0) = a`).
details: Covers every pair of 32-bit inputs a and b, interpreted as unsigned natural numbers for the greatest common divisor.
The returned greatest common divisor is reduced modulo 2 to the 32nd power; the claim specifies no signed interpretation or arithmetic wraparound during the gcd calculation itself.
Returns also guarantees the module is instantiable, and that every call in every fresh instance and host behavior terminates without trapping or throwing and returns exactly the specified result.
